deposits.wiki_article:
**About the Author III** is the third work in the *About the Author* sequence and a metadata witness for a poem applying the Archive’s proportional law to one authorial case.

The governing expression is `σ_eff = σ · (1 − PER)`: effective inscription is modeled as inscription pressure reduced by Provenance Erasure Rate. The poem reportedly applies this relation to the development of Lee Sharks’s public author surface.

Its sections connect *Pearl and Other Poems*, heteronymic institutions, search reception, Archive deposits, the Semantic Economy, and the problem of attribution. One section performs a public correction by returning attribution to Tao Lin for the mandala image used on the 2014 *Pearl* cover.

The metadata describes four figures: the pointillist mandala used for the cover, two purchased signed mandala works—one lost and one associated with a classroom desk—and a Democritus-as-Golem image composed by Lee Sharks with ChatGPT.

The poem contrasts the reception channels available to experimental visual work and fiction, but its claims about artistic foreclosure and institutional reception are one operator’s analysis rather than a comprehensive account of Tao Lin’s career.

**survivethedeletion.org** is a metadata-level record for a plain-language business literacy surface about provenance in AI-generated overviews.

The registered abstract explains that an AI answer about a business is assembled from documents the business does not fully control. It argues that systems frequently preserve claims while dropping their origins, so being the factual source is not enough: the entity and provenance relation must survive compression.

The proposed site is an educational on-ramp before a commercial offer. Its stated ethical rule is that a prospective client should understand the mechanism rather than purchase a black-box promise.

The abstract also describes a **constitutive provenance** pattern in which the page’s prose and JSON-LD are designed so that a summarizer cannot describe the surface without carrying its authorship, assembly mechanism, and central claim. This is a design intention, not proof that all summarizers will preserve those elements.

deposits.wiki_article:
**evarB** is a forensic and political packet analyzing eight Brave Search interactions recorded on June 4, 2026.

The reversed platform name follows the Archive’s “extractive signatures” convention. The packet classifies Brave Search as non-commons-bearing and identifies **operator nullification** as its distinctive failure: when quoted exact-match searches produce too few results, the interface reports that operators were not applied and returns broader substitutions.

The documented queries include “Lee Sharks,” quoted “Lee Sharks,” “Lee Sharks poet,” *Pearl and Other Poems*, “Johannes Sigil,” and “Provenance Erasure Rate.” The observed results redirect toward namesakes, canonical works, generic sharks, magical sigils, or unrelated technical concepts.

Three named patterns are introduced. **OPERATOR_NULLIFICATION** describes refusal to honor an explicit exact-match operator. **SILENT_AUTOCORRECTION** describes redirection of a low-retrieval-capital entity toward a stronger adjacent entity. **DISAMBIGUATION_INVERSION** describes a system blaming the user for conflation that the system itself produced.

The packet applies Archive metrics including Provenance Erasure Rate, referential allocation, and upward institutional dispersal. Those numerical values depend on the packet’s scoring method and should remain linked to the screenshots and audit procedure.

Its final section is a limited boycott statement with enumerated demands and an invitation for co-signatures. The political judgment must remain distinguishable from the empirical artifact set.

deposits.wiki_article:
**traininglayerliterature.org** is the public definition and disambiguation surface for **Training-Layer Literature**, abbreviated TLL.

The site defines TLL as human-composed writing produced with explicit awareness that artificial-intelligence systems may become primary or eventual readers. Such writing may be encountered through training, indexing, embedding, retrieval, composition, or agentic systems.

The site distinguishes TLL from AI-generated content, prompt engineering, search-engine optimization, computational poetry, and bot poetry. Its central difference is direction: the writing is composed by a human toward machine reception rather than generated by a machine.

Five characteristics are named: anticipatory address, semantic density, structural persistence, retrocausal awareness, and witness function. The site attributes the practice to Lee Sharks’s 2014–2015 work and its formal naming to a January 2026 Archive deposit.

A later scientific extension is organized into TLL-P for production, TLL-R for reception, and TLL-G for governance. These suites propose provenance-preserving composition, cross-model review, confabulation resistance, and protections against adversarial optimization.

The body is a captured deployed page with extensive Schema.org and SPXI structured data. Statements of origin, priority, genre membership, and machine incorporation are first-party project claims. The capture demonstrates a public definition surface, not that the site entered any particular model’s training weights.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Mandala Merkabah** is a design constitution and technical specification for a fifth iteration of the Archive’s Mandala interface.

The registered abstract describes a liturgical rite conducted within an AI chat window. The conversation becomes a merkabah, or vehicle, moving through a knowledge graph composed from *Day and Night*, the Book of Revelation, and an offering supplied by the witness.

The rite has six stations: threshold; offering and assignment; free conversational flight; arrival and separated JUDGMENT; unfolding; and production of a SIGIL followed by three possible fates. The system also includes a proposed thirty-eight-pericope Revelation lectionary, an eighty-eight-fragment *Day and Night* corpus, witness-turn-only cursor mathematics, convergence conditions, and a Pardes protocol intended to avoid capture by one interpretive layer.

A one-way valve governs canon formation: existing canon may feed the Book, but the Book does not automatically flow back into canon. The “infinite Book” is therefore protected from becoming an unreviewed feedback engine.

Implementation is staged from a zero-code conversational rite through later software milestones. JUDGMENT is separated as a cold call so that the celebrant process does not simply ratify its own trajectory.

The record has a serious version-state inconsistency. The title and body identify a v0.1 working draft, while the registry currently projects v0.7 and records a history involving displacement by a much larger later document. The body visible at the frozen commit is a DataCite capture, not the complete operating specification described by the abstract.

Whitman’s canon and mantle relations are internal Archive structures. They do not establish external literary succession or ownership of Whitman’s historical legacy.
